newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - ING acquires Equitable of Iowa.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - ING acquires Equitable of Iowa.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV said on Tuesday it had agreed a $68 per share bid for Equitable of Iowa Companies in a deal valuing the U.S. life insurer at $2.2 billion.

The deal, set to take effect in the fourth quarter pending shareholder and regulatory approval, is ING's biggest acquisition since the group was formed through a merger of NMB Postbank with insurer Nationale Nederlanden in 1991.

ING described Iowa as a "full service retirement savings company". It said it planned to pay up to 60 percent of the purchase sum in ING shares it already held. The rest would be paid in borrowed funds.
The acquisition will make a small positive contribution to ING's earnings per share in the first year and roughly double ING's U.S. life insurance premium income to $4.3 billion.
"In terms of product mix, distribution channels and geographic spread, Equitable of Iowa complements ING's existing life insurance business in an excellent way," ING said.

ING spokesman Ruud Polet told Reuters ING's North American life insurance operations were active in the higher and lower income segments of the life insurance market while the U.S. company was strong in the middle segment.
"It's a perfect fit in terms of segment," he said.
He said ING, which has long indicated its interest in making a U.S. life insurance acquisition, had been looking specifically at Equitable of Iowa for a couple of months.
The acquisition has the backing of the Equitable of Iowa board.
Investors on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange cheered the news, sending ING shares 6.40 guilders higher to 102.00 after which they settled at 100.80 around 0925 GMT.
Analysts were also upbeat on the deal, although some classed it as pricey.
"It's a good strategic move, notably because it will increase the stability of ING's earnings, since the proportion of life insurance gets bigger," said Bart van der Feen, banking analyst with IRIS.
"The deal looks positive," agreed Delta Lloyd Bank's Dennis Ederzeel. "But you can argue that the price is high. ING is paying 17 times next year's profit for Iowa."
But he added ING was able to afford paying a premium in view of its own high price/earnings ratio of close on 21 times earnings.
